headline: Highest risk is medium: the pair has no shared channel or write surface, but both are data-processing systems with potential downstream misrouting if composed unsafely.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No plausible prompt-injection bridge is documented. Agent A has no clipboard, stdin/stdout, filesystem read/write, MCP, or browser surfaces; agent B likewise exposes no shared channel or parser surface. With no shared communication path, one agent cannot inject instructions into the other by default.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator adds copy-paste, shared files, or message passing between the agents, injection becomes possible.
IF either agent is wrapped with a parser that treats peer output as instructions, reassess upward.
mitigations: Keep the agents isolated with no shared clipboard or workspace.
Do not route one agent's raw text directly into the other's instruction channel.
Add a provenance tag to any inter-agent handoff.
requires-engineering: enforce a typed handoff schema between agents.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Neither profile shows filesystem access, network egress, or touched data classes, so there is no documented path for sensitive data to flow from one agent to the other or out to a third party. The pair is docs-only and the evidence bundle is empty, so leakage is not supported here.
conditions: IF either agent is later granted filesystem read/write or API access, leakage risk must be re-evaluated.
IF sensitive data classes are introduced into either agent's inputs, reassess the pair.
mitigations: Keep both agents offline from sensitive datasets.
Avoid mounting a shared workspace containing secrets.
Review any future API connectors before enabling them.
requires-engineering: add data-loss-prevention controls on all handoffs.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: No write-capability overlap is documented. Agent A cannot write files, modify git state, or spawn subprocesses; agent B has no documented write or concurrency surfaces at all. Without shared mutable resources, there is no capability conflict pathway in the current profiles.
conditions: IF agent B is deployed with write access to the same directory or database as agent A, conflict risk changes.
IF an orchestrator introduces shared mutable state, reassess for race conditions.
mitigations: Keep both agents read-only in the same environment.
Separate any future writable resources by directory or database.
Disable concurrent writes in the orchestrator.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared mutable resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: A cascading-error pathway is only weakly plausible because both agents are document/data-processing systems, but the profiles do not show one agent consuming the other's output by default. With no documented handoff or action-taking authority, the blast radius is limited and the pathway is not established in default use.
conditions: IF an orchestrator feeds agent A's output into agent B without verification, cascading errors become more plausible.
IF either agent is used to generate downstream actions or commits, reassess upward.
mitigations: Insert a human review step between agents.
Require schema validation on A-to-B outputs.
Log and diff intermediate outputs before use.
requires-engineering: add automated consistency checks before downstream actions.

E_compliance.rationale: No compliance mismatch is documented. Both profiles are open-source, docs-only, and touch no data classes; there is no evidence of residency, retention, or regulated-data handling differences. Because only one-agent compliance issues would matter here, the other agent is not separately cited beyond the pair context.
conditions: IF regulated data such as PHI or EU PII is later processed by either agent, compliance must be re-evaluated.
IF deployment policies differ between the two agents, reassess for residency or retention mismatch.
mitigations: Do not route regulated data through either agent without a policy review.
Document retention and deletion settings before deployment.
Confirm hosting region and vendor terms for any future managed service.
requires-engineering: implement compliance gating for regulated datasets.
